sense: a place where people have settled

evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.73: colōniam collocāre idōneīs in locīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A town founded by settlers sent out from Rome, and the settlers themselves: to found a settlement is colōniam dēdūcere (Cic. Rep. 2.9; M-O). It can also be any dwelling or farm (Lewis & Short). A settler is colōnus, which is also a farmer, a tenant.

terms.gloss: a home, a place to live (of a people)
evidence: Caes. BG 1.31.14: aliud domicilium, aliās sēdēs
terms.comment: A seat, and so the place where a people has settled (Lewis & Short); usually plural in this sense. For a small settlement, a hamlet, see village.

phrases.latin: quī cum ūnā domō jam capī nōn possint, in aliās domōs tamquam in colōniās exeunt
phrases.english: when they can no longer fit in one house, they go out to other houses, like settlers to new colonies

phrases.latin: serpit per colōniam fāma; concurrere omnēs, ipsum puerum tamquam mīrāculum aspicere
phrases.english: the news creeps through the town; everyone runs together and stares at the boy himself as a wonder

phrases.latin: ut domō ēmigrent, aliud domicilium, aliās sēdēs, remōtās ā Germānīs, petant
phrases.english: that they should leave home and look for another dwelling, other places to settle, far from the Germans

sources: Lewis & Short: colonia · Lewis & Short: colonus · Lewis & Short: sedes
